$comment: Maintained platform list. NEUTRALITY RULES: describe, never endorse. This site lists providers, it does not recommend them, it is affiliated with none of them, and it takes no payment. verification must be one of: official (named as an SC-accredited ENF provider in a primary Supreme Court document — as of 7 August 2026 the only such document is the SC's own ENP Application Form, ENP Form 1 (2026), which asks lawyer-applicants to select the SC-accredited ENF provider they are enrolled with and lists exactly three; a form is NOT a promulgated register, the SC has published no standalone list page, and its public directory of accredited facility providers still reads AVAILABLE SOON) | self-reported (claims it, and no source we have seen names it) | unverified | not-applicable. Being absent from that form is not evidence that a provider is not accredited — accreditation applications have been open since 9 December 2025 and are rolling, and accreditation can lapse or be revoked. It is a fact about a provider on a given date. No paid placement, ever. Philippine providers are ordered alphabetically, not by preference; the us-platforms row is kept last because it exists to explain an absence rather than to list a competitor.

platforms.name: eNotary Philippines
platforms.notes: Not among the three ENF providers named in the Supreme Court's own ENP Application Form (ENP Form 1 (2026)), checked 7 August 2026. That absence is not proof it is unaccredited — it means we can point to no official document naming it. We have seen no pricing or accreditation evidence published. Ask for the Certificate of Accreditation before paying.

platforms.name: NotarialOS
platforms.notes: Publishes a flat consumer price. It is not among the three ENF providers named in the Supreme Court's own ENP Application Form (ENP Form 1 (2026)), checked 7 August 2026 — and a published price is not evidence of accreditation. That absence is not proof it is unaccredited; it means we can point to no official document naming it. Ask for the Certificate of Accreditation before paying.

platforms.name: QLegal (Quanby Legal)
platforms.who: Individuals and businesses; markets round-the-clock online sessions
platforms.modes: States it supports both remote (REN) and in-person (IEN) notarization
platforms.pricing: Not published — advertises a free tier and enterprise pricing on request
platforms.notes: Operated by Quanby Solutions, Inc. Listed as "Qlegal (Quanby Solutions, Inc.)" in the Supreme Court's official ENP Application Form (ENP Form 1 (2026)), one of exactly three SC-accredited ENF providers an applying lawyer may select. The source is an application form, not a promulgated register, and it carries no accreditation date — so we cannot tell you when it was accredited. Also named in PhilSTAR L!fe reporting of 5 August 2026. States it supports both remote and in-person sessions. No per-document consumer price is published; the site advertises a free subscription tier and custom enterprise pricing. Ask for the Certificate of Accreditation yourself before paying.

platforms.name: Twala
platforms.who: Businesses and law offices; e-signature workflows
platforms.modes: States it supports electronic notarization workflows
platforms.notes: Operated by Ohelio, Inc. Listed as "Twala (Ohelio, Inc.)" in the Supreme Court's official ENP Application Form (ENP Form 1 (2026)), one of exactly three SC-accredited ENF providers an applying lawyer may select. The source is an application form, not a promulgated register, and it carries no accreditation date. Also named in PhilSTAR L!fe reporting of 5 August 2026. A partnership with the Integrated Bar of the Philippines was announced through PR channels in January 2026 — a bar-association partnership is not accreditation and is not an endorsement by the IBP or the Court. Ask for the Certificate of Accreditation yourself before paying.

platforms.name: UNAWA NotarizeIT
platforms.who: Businesses, law firms, enterprise document flows
platforms.modes: States it supports remote electronic notarization
platforms.notes: Operated by UNAWA, Inc. Listed as "NotarizeIT (UNAWA, Inc.)" in the Supreme Court's official ENP Application Form (ENP Form 1 (2026)), one of exactly three SC-accredited ENF providers an applying lawyer may select. The source is an application form, not a promulgated register, and it carries no accreditation date. Also named in PhilSTAR L!fe reporting of 5 August 2026. Its own site stated on 7 August 2026 that it is still completing Supreme Court registrations for commissioned notaries before opening document notarization to the general public — so being accredited does not mean you can use it today. Ask for the Certificate of Accreditation yourself before paying.

platforms.name: Notarize.com, DocuSign Notary and other US platforms
platforms.notes: Included so nobody is misled. These platforms operate under US state RON laws. They are not Philippine electronic notarization and their output is not a Philippine notarized document.

howToChoose: Ask the platform to show you its Certificate of Accreditation from the Supreme Court, and check the name against reporting you can date and attribute. Accreditation is a fact about a provider on a given date, not a permanent property — re-check it yourself rather than relying on any list, including this one.
Ask whether the e-notary who will handle your document holds an Electronic Notary Public commission, and ask for their roll number.
Ask what the total price is, including VAT and any per-signatory charges, before you upload anything.
Check that the platform requires each signatory to create their own account. A platform happy to let several people share one login is not following the Rules.

Walk away from any platform that offers to notarize while you are sitting at home abroad. Under the Rules that is not allowed, and a platform that offers it is telling you something important about itself.
